messages:
sara: Heads up 10AM call with Acme to propose a migration POC from RivalAI. They want near-drop-in parity, clear cost comparison, and checklist for security/legal. Can we sketch a playbook here?

ben: Quick notes: Rival does streaming token-by-token and injects metadata in event boundaries. Our streaming API is chunked and can drop trailing whitespace differences. Need to test stream framing.

mia: I can run an end-to-end shim. Plan: 1) Rival -> Redwood adapter that accepts Rival params, 2) run canonical prompts and real app traces, 3) compare outputs and parse failures, 4) provide remediation (normalizer, pre/post processors).

raj: Tokenization: Rival uses a variant BPE that splits some punctuation differently -> prompts that hit token limits on Rival may exceed on Redwood or vice versa. Add a token-estimator step in shim that adjusts `max_tokens`.

anya: Security: they sent an NDA + 30-question security checklist. Key asks: no retention of eval data, customer-managed keys for Private, and audit logs. We can do ephemeral workspace + retention disabled for POC but need SRE approval.

infra-bot: ephemeral env created: acme-poc-2026 (expires in 6 days). Staging endpoints: https://staging.reddemo/acme-poc. Secrets rotated every 12h.

oliver: Pricing ask: show hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved. Scenario: 800k messages/month, avg 120 generated tokens. Also run a worst-case burst (200 QPS sustained for 2 mins).

mia: For the POC deliverables: (A) parity report (token diffs, text diffs, schema validation rate), (B) failure log with examples and suggested normalizer rules, (C) streaming/latency comparison, (D) cost model.

ben: Also watch function-calling and structured output differences. Rival returns `fields` within `choices[*].metadata` sometimes; our SDK returns structured JSON under `output`. The shim should remap keys and preserve status codes for downstream ingesters.

raj: Edge case: Rival strips trailing commas in arrays, while some clients depended on them. Add an "emulate-rival" toggle in normalizer to replicate these quirks during testing.

anya: I'll own the SSAQ answers and confirm retention toggles. Please DM me the checklist PDF and any network/dataflow diagrams.

mia: ETA: initial adapter + prompt run in 48 hours, full report in 5 business days.

oliver: I'll create the hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison. If they need SLA for 95p latency, call out Dedicated as path to contractual SLA; for POC we can report measured numbers only.

sara: Acceptance criteria to propose to Acme: 1) >=98% schema-valid responses for sample set, 2) top-1 text diff rate <5% for deterministic prompts (temp=0), 3) observed 95th lat < their threshold in staging, 4) security checklist answered and retention mode verified.

ben: Operational blockers: stream framing, rate-limit backoff semantics differ (Rival does per-client tokens per minute). We should emulate Rival's backoff to match client behavior during the POC.

mia: Will include a small JS shim example in the repo and a docker image for their devs to try locally.

anya: Once the adapter is up, I'll test with their sample payloads and mark items in the SSAQ.

sara: Good. I'll intro Marie (Acme eng) on the call and send the acceptance criteria. Follow-ups: infra-bot please document workspace creds and expiration in the thread.

infra-bot: workspace docs: https://internal/staging/acme-poc-2026; creds expire 2026-06-02T07:00Z.

mia: assigning tasks: adapter + harness (mia), prompt corpus (raj), pricing (oliver), SSAQ (anya), stream checks (ben). I'll post the initial test gist in 24h.

sara: Thanks team 1: will prep the slide for the 10AM call and iterate after the POC results. :thumbsup:
